title: Determinism at the Boundary: Keeping AI Out of the Compute Path — Check

questions.prompt: Why is Agronomy Studio's AI search implemented as a deterministic mock in this build?
questions.explanation: Determinism makes tests meaningful and lets every reported value be re-derived from the same inputs — the system stays trustworthy.
options: Because deterministic behavior keeps the pipeline testable and the reported results reproducible
Because LLMs are too expensive to call even once
Because Netlify does not allow network calls
Because the frontend cannot parse model output

questions.prompt: In the recommended design, what role does AI play relative to the deterministic core?
questions.explanation: AI lives outside the compute path — converting user text to a structured query or summarizing output — while correctness-critical work stays deterministic.
options: It performs the core classification and aggregation
It sits at the edge in an advisory role, e.g. turning text into a structured query
It validates that the deterministic results are correct

questions.prompt: Because the AI boundary is an explicit contract (a structured query), the stub can later be replaced by a real LLM without changing the trusted deterministic core.
questions.explanation: The structured query is the contract between the AI edge and the core, so swapping the stub for a real model leaves the deterministic logic untouched.
